scope: Direct read of 27 Gurbāṇī readers and one Nānak-attributed inclusion candidate; 608 performed definitions / 3199 word entries. Every no-change result follows a concrete source/gloss/English reading. Original whole-library task remains open beyond this group.
rootCause: Prior reference review followed a finite detector and existing tag examples too closely; explicit Brahmā/Indra and specific Nṛsiṃha were missed. Broad screened labels then obscured incomplete reference coverage. Grammar/word-link errors also survived those labels. The song procedure now explicitly requires named-reference inventory beyond the detector list.

songs.reading: l001–l010: opening Gurū invocations and actual names Nānak Dev/Gobind Siṅgh; Gobind in the latter is a human name, not deity evidence. l019–l026: Gobind, Rām, Dāmodar and Mādhav are actual divine invocations; retain Guru/Rāma/Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu. Dāmodar supplies concrete Kṛṣṇa identity independently of generic lord titles. l031–l050: read renunciation teaching in full: forest/home comparison, chastity as locks, spiritual discipline as bath, observance as nails, knowledge as teacher, name as ashes, compassion and forgiveness, three qualities, rejection of vices, self and Supreme Being. l045 tan=with/toward is explicitly supported by Mahan Kosh quoting this line; do not change to body. l025 bodily health/decline and l026 prayer may Nanak remember agree with Sahib Singh.

All 21 records read, including thread/beads, warp/weft, one/many, māiā pictures, water/waves/foam/bubbles, manifest world as play, dream objects falsely taken as permanent, Guru instruction and awakened mind. Gobind, Hari, Murārī occur as source names; Murārī at keval-ek-murari explicitly supports Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu despite universal divine context. Sukrit mansā=good understanding and bicrat=on reflection are confirmed in Sahib Singh. Existing translation retains concrete images; no text change needed.

All 11 records read: prayer to master, life/body as capital, mother/father and children, grace, immeasurability, creation/thread, obedience, nature/extent, sacrifice, Vāhigurū. Bhagvant and Ṭhākur are generic divine titles here; mother/father are relational metaphors, not named Śakti/Śiva references. No new deity tags warranted. Guru supported by performed Vāhigurū, existing Nirguṇa consistent with boundless divine description. Rāsi capital/entrusted stock retains material metaphor; sūtri thread retains concrete image underlying command/order interpretation.

All eight records read, including repeated Nānak begs. Divine sweetness, request for Name, inward meditation, ferrying companions, Guru at side, repeated remembrance all remain intact. Dhiāī/tarāī first-person interpretation is supported by Sahib Singh; do not replace with second-person imperative merely because one English version does. Hari supports existing Viṣṇu name reference; no specific Kṛṣṇa episode or exclusive epithet in this text. Existing Guru explicit in gur-merai-sang-sada-hai-naale. No tag change proposed.

All 48 records read, including performance fragments/repeated lines and appended longing verses. Cātaka/rainbird cry, thirst, face/speech, separation as dark age, sleeplessness, Guru reunion, arrow in heart, unknowable pain, waiting bride, tears/sighs/unmoving foot, opened doors retained. line-007 Śārṅgapāṇi identifies bow-bearing Viṣṇu; line-009/011 Murāri identifies enemy of Mura and supports Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu. Generic manohara, bride and dark age do not independently support further tags. line-019 guri is agentive and santu the peaceful divine one in Sahib Singh; current Guru united me with holy one and its clarifying gloss accurately preserve this. Final source comparison resolves line-040 as the adjective bharīle, filled with tears, not separate le meaning draws. Source and Roman token units retained, with joint gloss/link and accurate grammar note.

songs.reading: All 37 records read including expanded repeated refrain; drowning/swimming/rescuing arm image retained. g010/g017 Bīṭhulā is Viṭṭhala, the divine father invoked as Rāma in this same prayer. Proposed Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu tags record the named form and its identity, not an assertion of idol worship; Sahib Singh explicitly reads the prayer as addressed to God. g018–g025 human becoming god and conquering heaven with remedy of Guru-given understanding retained. Pāī may I obtain is supported by Sahib Singh. g028–g036 Dhruva and Nārada actually named and preserved; source narrative asks same stable spiritual condition. Naiku for ever follows explicit Sahib Singh derivation from Sanskrit naikaś/repeatedly and Punjabi sadā; no correction to a moment is justified merely by English variant.

songs.reading: 25 definitions read, including repeated fragments. Rām Dās is the fourth Sikh Guru, Nānak/Lehṇā/Amar Dās refer to Guru continuity. Pārbrahm is supreme divine reality, not Brahmā. Creator placing Himself within the Guru, vice-family driven out, unweighable depth, congregation and steady mind checked against Darpan 968. Vāhigurū adds no separate deity form.

All 14 definitions read: daily rising/bath/nectar pool, repeated Hari recitation, breath and morsel, Guru instruction and disciple dust. Hari named; existing Viṣṇu/Guru retained. Nānak is signature; no Kṛṣṇa inferred solely from explanatory Hari gloss. Nectar pool retained literally, with Darpan interpreting the Name metaphor.

All 10 definitions read: self-sale, Hari sight, grace, comfort/pain, being sated in hunger, body/mind cutting, fire, fan/water service, threshold and favor. Full source Darpan 757 confirms rājā as being sated and vaḍiāī as favor. Performed kare/mele variant retained; no source/transcription change. Existing Guru/Viṣṇu cover explicit named references.

All 21 definitions read, including complete refrain and fragments. Bride/virtue, Guru Word dye/piercing, dye-vat, directions, friends failing and Beloved meeting, truth as capital/earnings all considered. Generic True One/Prabh/Beloved does not name an additional deity form; no tag addition. Darpan 37 supports all-pervading bharpūri, dye-vat raṅgaṇi and expectation behind making friends. Clarified English purpose clause only.

tagAdditions.reason: Rājā Dharam is Dharma-rāja/Yama, the personified judge singing at the divine door. The adjacent Citra/Gupta records establish the tribunal context; Sahib Singh explains the named judge as Yamarāja. This is not an inference from generic death.

songs.reading: Read sorrow/joy remembrance couplet and exhortation to mind; life passing without Hari name. Read well/water, cow/milk, earth/cloud, tree/fruit, body/eyes, night/moon, temple/lamp, scholar/Vedas analogies, lust/anger/pride/greed renunciation, Nānak Śāh signature and no worldly own companion. The performed Hindi compilation matches popular Sumiran Kar Le material in Ashram Bhajanavali; Guru credit/signature alone is insufficient to certify canonical Gurbāṇī. Retain current Nirguṇa, Viṣṇu classification.

uncertainties: Canonical Gurbāṇī identity has not been established. Do not add Gurbāṇī solely from Nānak Śāh signature or poet credit. Poem is demonstrably circulated in bhajan anthologies; no claim that it is absent from every Sikh corpus.
